policy.purpose: Complete five-depth menu assignment requested by the user; not a claim that all initial-access histories are established
policy.victimBoundary: Always state whose action and which scenario boundary the displayed depth describes
policy.selectedScenario: A named supported variant can place a multi-route campaign; retain the narrower scope prominently
policy.editorialPlacement: When required by the complete menu, uncertain records get an explicit editorial placement and badge; never infer zero action from missing evidence
policy.referencePlacement: Disclosures/display-risk references have a depth-related library position, not an invented attack mechanism
policy.sourcePreservation: Keep historical facts/confidence, original subtype/SEV, and the stricter evidence-only placement separately
policy.integration: Classification only; original source catalogues, renderer bundles and sandbox behaviours remain unchanged

entries.name: Melissa
entries.victimPerspective: Employee opening the infected Word document
entries.rationale: Attachment-driven macro execution enables automated mass mailing; propagation is the dominant lesson.
entries.evidenceRationale: Attachment-driven macro execution enables automated mass mailing; propagation is the dominant lesson.

entries.name: ILOVEYOU (Love Bug)
entries.victimPerspective: Recipient opening the script attachment
entries.rationale: User execution starts the mass-mailing worm; overwriting and credential theft remain secondary consequences.
entries.evidenceRationale: User execution starts the mass-mailing worm; overwriting and credential theft remain secondary consequences.

entries.name: Mydoom
entries.victimPerspective: Recipient executing the email-delivered worm
entries.rationale: Classified on the documented email-attachment execution route, not every peer-to-peer variant.
entries.evidenceRationale: Classified on the documented email-attachment execution route, not every peer-to-peer variant.

entries.name: Emotet
entries.victimPerspective: Recipient opening a malicious attachment
entries.rationale: Classified on the sourced malicious-file execution variant. Its coordinated delivery platform is primary; do not imply every Emotet link causes one-click execution.
entries.evidenceRationale: Classified on the sourced malicious-file execution variant. Its coordinated delivery platform is primary; do not imply every Emotet link causes one-click execution.

entries.name: RSA SecurID
entries.victimPerspective: RSA employee targeted at the authentication supplier
entries.rationale: Reporting describes an Excel attachment with an embedded exploit. The supplier-trust lesson is primary; do not claim a precise token-seed scope or every downstream customer compromised.
entries.evidenceRationale: Reporting describes an Excel attachment with an embedded exploit. The supplier-trust lesson is primary; do not claim a precise token-seed scope or every downstream customer compromised.

entries.name: Anthem
entries.victimPerspective: Employee of the affected Anthem subsidiary
entries.classificationScope: Malware-file delivery/execution story from the indictment
entries.rationale: The indictment describes a link, file download and execution, without establishing whether an employee separately executed the file. Sunlight is the editorial best fit for the file-execution story, not a verified manual launch.
entries.evidenceRationale: The indictment distinguishes clicking a hyperlink, downloading a file and executing it. It does not establish whether the victim separately ran the file; one-click-only and manual-file execution are both unproven.

entries.name: Carbanak (Anunak)
entries.victimPerspective: Bank employee targeted by a malicious attachment
entries.rationale: The described attachment route enables later banking and ATM theft; the theft operation is the dominant story.
entries.evidenceRationale: The described attachment route enables later banking and ATM theft; the theft operation is the dominant story.

entries.name: PC Cyborg (AIDS Trojan)
entries.victimPerspective: Recipient running the AIDS-information disk program
entries.rationale: Running the delivered program is required; later reboot counting and ransom demands are consequences.
entries.evidenceRationale: Running the delivered program is required; later reboot counting and ransom demands are consequences.

entries.name: Ukrainian power grid
entries.victimPerspective: Affected Ukrainian power-grid operator
entries.rationale: The attachment infection is reported, but CISA did not establish its role in the grid intrusion. Sunlight illustrates that delivery story; it is not proof that opening the document caused the outage.
entries.evidenceRationale: CISA confirms remote breaker operation and disruption but says BlackEnergy's initial-access role was still under evaluation. Do not convert a reported attachment infection into a proven outage-entry gate.

entries.name: LAPSUS$ (Okta / Microsoft / T-Mobile / Uber)
entries.victimPerspective: Employee responding to attacker-induced MFA prompts
entries.classificationScope: Documented MFA-fatigue/approval variant, not every LAPSUS$ incident
entries.rationale: Use the employee MFA-approval scenario documented within the campaign. Purchased credentials, help-desk and SIM-swap variants retain their own different interaction requirements.
entries.evidenceRationale: The entry combines MFA fatigue, help-desk deception, SIM swapping and purchased credentials. No single required action is established for the whole combined campaign.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ

entries.name: Smishing / parcel lure (2010s)
entries.victimPerspective: SMS recipient entering credentials at the spoofed site
entries.rationale: For the credential-page variant described in the entry, following the link alone does not disclose credentials; submission is the decisive action.
entries.evidenceRationale: For the credential-page variant described in the entry, following the link alone does not disclose credentials; submission is the decisive action.

entries.name: Quishing (QR-code phishing)
entries.victimPerspective: QR-code recipient submitting credentials to the spoofed site
entries.rationale: For the described credential-stealing-site variant, scanning/navigation alone is not credential theft. Classify credential submission, not the preliminary QR scan.
entries.evidenceRationale: For the described credential-stealing-site variant, scanning/navigation alone is not credential theft. Classify credential submission, not the preliminary QR scan.

entries.name: Zeus (Zbot)
entries.victimPerspective: Banking user whose browser is already compromised
entries.classificationScope: Banking-form credential-capture scenario, not initial malware installation
entries.rationale: The displayed boundary is entering banking credentials into a browser modified by Zeus. Initial installation remains a separate, unresolved question.
entries.evidenceRationale: Typing a banking password after infection is not initial access. The broad malware entry does not establish one required installation route.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ

entries.name: Collection #1 (credential compilation)
entries.victimPerspective: No single newly compromised victim represented by the compilation
entries.rationale: The compiled credential collection belongs beside password-related lessons. It is not a fresh attack or proof that a victim submitted a password in 2019.
entries.evidenceRationale: A compilation of previously exposed credentials is a disclosure, not a fresh intrusion with an established interaction gate.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Reference entry — not a victim-compromise classification

entries.name: Lookalike / IDN homograph domains
entries.victimPerspective: Browser user inspecting an apparent origin
entries.rationale: The browser-display risk is encountered while navigating to an apparent origin. This is a reference placement, not a claim that navigation itself steals credentials.
entries.evidenceRationale: This standalone record describes an address-bar spoofing risk, not a completed credential leak or a single compromise gate. Keep it in reference material rather than inventing a breach depth.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Reference entry — not a victim-compromise classification

entries.name: Crypto drainer kits (wallet-approval phishing)
entries.victimPerspective: Wallet holder signing the malicious approval
entries.rationale: The described gate is a wallet authorisation/signature, not supplying an OTP or recovery secret. Keep the high financial impact separate from depth.
entries.evidenceRationale: The described gate is a wallet authorisation/signature, not supplying an OTP or recovery secret. Keep the high financial impact separate from depth.

entries.name: OAuth consent phishing (AiTM precursor, category)
entries.victimPerspective: User granting the malicious connected app access
entries.rationale: The consent-only variant grants access without a fake login, password capture, extra authentication-factor disclosure or downloaded-file execution.
entries.evidenceRationale: The consent-only variant grants access without a fake login, password capture, extra authentication-factor disclosure or downloaded-file execution.

entries.name: Business Email Compromise (invoice thread)
entries.victimPerspective: Finance recipient persuaded to authorise a fraudulent payment
entries.classificationScope: Finance-victim transaction boundary, not mailbox initial access
entries.rationale: Classify the entry's invoice/payment authorisation boundary, not an invented initial compromise of the existing email thread. No attacker-directed credential disclosure or file execution is specified.
entries.evidenceRationale: Classify the entry's invoice/payment authorisation boundary, not an invented initial compromise of the existing email thread. No attacker-directed credential disclosure or file execution is specified.

entries.name: Salesforce / UNC6040 vishing
entries.victimPerspective: Employee approving the malicious connected app
entries.rationale: Voice persuasion leads to application authorisation without password theft; data export follows the consent boundary.
entries.evidenceRationale: Voice persuasion leads to application authorisation without password theft; data export follows the consent boundary.

entries.name: SIM swap / SMS OTP interception
entries.victimPerspective: Subscriber whose number is reassigned
entries.rationale: In the selected carrier-impersonation variant, the attacker persuades carrier staff and receives redirected codes. The subscriber does not provide the code or approve MFA. Carrier employees are a different perspective.
entries.evidenceRationale: In the selected carrier-impersonation variant, the attacker persuades carrier staff and receives redirected codes. The subscriber does not provide the code or approve MFA. Carrier employees are a different perspective.

entries.name: Heartbleed
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of the vulnerable TLS service
entries.rationale: Remote heartbeat handling can expose process memory without a victim response.
entries.evidenceRationale: Remote heartbeat handling can expose process memory without a victim response.

entries.name: Yahoo forged cookies 2015–16
entries.victimPerspective: Yahoo account holder targeted by a forged session
entries.rationale: Forged cookies allow attacker access without the account holder supplying a password or responding.
entries.evidenceRationale: Forged cookies allow attacker access without the account holder supplying a password or responding.

entries.name: Equifax
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of the exposed Equifax web application
entries.rationale: Server-side exploitation of the unpatched application needs no victim response; data theft is a secondary outcome.
entries.evidenceRationale: Server-side exploitation of the unpatched application needs no victim response; data theft is a secondary outcome.

entries.name: Capital One (WAF misconfiguration, SSRF)
entries.victimPerspective: Capital One cloud-environment operator
entries.rationale: The documented server-side request/misconfiguration route needs no victim response; exposed credentials are obtained by the attacker, not typed by the victim.
entries.evidenceRationale: The documented server-side request/misconfiguration route needs no victim response; exposed credentials are obtained by the attacker, not typed by the victim.

entries.name: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228)
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of an application evaluating attacker-controlled logged input
entries.rationale: The server-side lookup flaw can be triggered by attacker input without a victim response.
entries.evidenceRationale: The server-side lookup flaw can be triggered by attacker input without a victim response.

entries.name: SharePoint ToolShell (CVE-2025-53770)
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of the exposed on-premises SharePoint server
entries.rationale: Unauthenticated requests trigger server-side exploitation without a victim response; key theft is a consequence, not a user credential submission.
entries.evidenceRationale: Unauthenticated requests trigger server-side exploitation without a victim response; key theft is a consequence, not a user credential submission.

entries.name: Blaster (MSBlast)
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of an exposed Windows host
entries.rationale: Remote service exploitation propagates without a victim click or file execution.
entries.evidenceRationale: Remote service exploitation propagates without a victim click or file execution.

entries.name: SQL Slammer
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of a vulnerable SQL Server
entries.rationale: The network-service worm needs no victim response; scanning congestion is the outcome.
entries.evidenceRationale: The network-service worm needs no victim response; scanning congestion is the outcome.

entries.name: Sasser worm
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of an exposed Windows host
entries.rationale: LSASS exploitation and network scanning do not require a victim response.
entries.evidenceRationale: LSASS exploitation and network scanning do not require a victim response.

entries.name: Conficker
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of a vulnerable Windows network host
entries.rationale: The selected MS08-067 network-service propagation route requires no victim response; removable-media and share variants are not silently assigned this depth.
entries.evidenceRationale: The selected MS08-067 network-service propagation route requires no victim response; removable-media and share variants are not silently assigned this depth.

entries.name: Mirai
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of an internet-connected device
entries.rationale: The selected self-propagating IoT botnet route does not require its owner to submit a password or respond to a lure.
entries.evidenceRationale: The selected self-propagating IoT botnet route does not require its owner to submit a password or respond to a lure.

entries.name: VPNFilter
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of the compromised router or NAS
entries.classificationScope: Network-device compromise story; individual infection route unconfirmed
entries.rationale: The implant affects routers/NAS devices, making deep the menu best fit. Talos was unsure of the exploit used in a given case; no specific default-password or zero-action route is asserted.
entries.evidenceRationale: Talos states it was unsure of the particular exploit used in any given case. Known exploits and default credentials are possibilities, not a proven interaction classification.

entries.name: Target
entries.victimPerspective: Target organisation, not the supplier employee opening an email
entries.rationale: The attacker uses the compromised supplier relationship. Deep is the best-fit downstream menu placement, but the partially unresolved access path does not establish a complete no-action history.
entries.evidenceRationale: Vendor credential theft and downstream POS theft are established; the curated record leaves the access path partly unresolved. Do not assign the vendor employee's email action to Target.

entries.name: NotPetya (M.E.Doc updater)
entries.victimPerspective: Organisation receiving the compromised M.E.Doc updater payload
entries.rationale: Classified on the updater-delivery mechanism, not a fictitious tax-document lure. It does not generalise no-action entry to every manually installed package.
entries.evidenceRationale: Classified on the updater-delivery mechanism, not a fictitious tax-document lure. It does not generalise no-action entry to every manually installed package.

entries.name: SolarWinds / SUNBURST
entries.victimPerspective: Downstream Orion customer organisation
entries.rationale: The signed build/update channel carries the payload. Classify the downstream updater/runtime compromise, not an invented human deception step at the supplier.
entries.evidenceRationale: The signed build/update channel carries the payload. Classify the downstream updater/runtime compromise, not an invented human deception step at the supplier.

entries.name: TJX (T.J. Maxx / Marshalls)
entries.victimPerspective: TJX store and corporate-network operators
entries.rationale: Classified on the reported external wireless-entry route; no employee response is required by that route. Reporting describes the route cautiously.
entries.evidenceRationale: Classified on the reported external wireless-entry route; no employee response is required by that route. Reporting describes the route cautiously.

entries.name: US Office of Personnel Management
entries.victimPerspective: OPM organisation, not an assumed contractor phishing victim
entries.rationale: The compromised contractor identity supports a deep organisational-access layout. Credential acquisition and any earlier human action remain unresolved; the placement is editorial, not proof of zero interaction.
entries.evidenceRationale: The KeyPoint credential was compromised, but how it was obtained was not determined. A compromised credential is neither proof of victim password submission nor proof of no victim action.

entries.name: Vault 7
entries.victimPerspective: No conventional victim compromise represented by this entry
entries.rationale: This is an editorial reference-library position for the disclosed cyber-tool inventory. There is no conventional victim-compromise depth to assert.
entries.evidenceRationale: A published inventory/disclosure is not a documented initial-access event. Its historical placement must not become a no-action attack.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Reference entry — not a victim-compromise classification

entries.name: Marriott / Starwood
entries.victimPerspective: Marriott/Starwood organisation
entries.classificationScope: Editorial deep placement for the persistent organisation breach
entries.rationale: Installation of the initial web shell was not determined. Deep groups the organisation-level intrusion story but does not resolve its entry method.
entries.evidenceRationale: The source explicitly leaves installation of the initial web shell undetermined; later tools and stolen data do not establish the entry interaction.

entries.name: LastPass (2022)
entries.victimPerspective: Engineer endpoint at the selected remote-exploitation stage
entries.rationale: The selected stage is remote exploitation of third-party media software on the engineer endpoint, before the keylogger captures later authentication. Do not classify that later password entry as the initial RCE gate.
entries.evidenceRationale: The entry combines two compromises. Third-party exploitation and later secret access are documented, but this combined record does not establish one decisive victim-action gate. Do not place later authentication at initial access.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ

entries.name: MOVEit / Cl0p (CVE-2023-34362)
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of the exposed MOVEit Transfer application
entries.rationale: Unauthenticated application exploitation enables bulk data theft. Retain SQL injection as a technique badge rather than losing the exfiltration lesson.
entries.evidenceRationale: Unauthenticated application exploitation enables bulk data theft. Retain SQL injection as a technique badge rather than losing the exfiltration lesson.

entries.name: AT&T (third-party cloud workspace)
entries.victimPerspective: AT&T cloud-workspace victim
entries.classificationScope: Editorial deep placement for the cloud-workspace exfiltration story
entries.rationale: The curated sources do not establish initial access. Deep is a workspace-compromise layout choice, not a proven no-action attack or a claim that a particular password attack occurred.
entries.evidenceRationale: Exfiltration from the workspace is documented, but the cited record does not establish how initial access was obtained.

entries.name: National Public Data / Infobroker
entries.victimPerspective: National Public Data organisation
entries.classificationScope: Editorial deep placement for the alleged data-broker breach
entries.rationale: The initial entry mechanism remains unconfirmed. The menu position reflects the organisation-level data-theft story and must carry that uncertainty badge.
entries.evidenceRationale: The public record cited in the catalogue does not establish a specific entry mechanism; do not equate an alleged data release with no-action access.

entries.name: Stuxnet
entries.victimPerspective: Owner of a host reached through network-service propagation
entries.classificationScope: Remote-service network-propagation variant, not first entry into the industrial target
entries.rationale: The selected network-service propagation route does not require a fresh response from the receiving host owner. Do not present this as the known first entry into Natanz.
entries.evidenceRationale: Industrial process manipulation is the dominant lesson. USB/network propagation does not establish the initial compromise path into the selected industrial victim.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ

entries.name: Shamoon (Disttrack)
entries.victimPerspective: Saudi Aramco corporate-network victim
entries.classificationScope: Editorial deep placement for an established destructive incident
entries.rationale: Initial access is unresolved. Trench is a menu-layout fallback for the system-level destructive story, not evidence that the victim did nothing.
entries.evidenceRationale: The cited description establishes wiping and disruption, not the decisive initial-access interaction. Destruction is not proof of no-action entry.

entries.name: Sony Pictures
entries.victimPerspective: Sony Pictures organisation
entries.classificationScope: Editorial deep placement for the destructive/data-theft incident
entries.rationale: The public source does not establish initial access. This position must carry an entry-route-unconfirmed badge and must not be described as proven zero-action entry.
entries.evidenceRationale: Observed destruction, theft and threats make destructive/extortion impact primary. The FBI statement does not establish initial access.

entries.name: WannaCry (WanaCrypt0r)
entries.victimPerspective: Operator of a vulnerable SMB service
entries.rationale: Wormable service exploitation enables encryption without a victim click, password submission or file launch.
entries.evidenceRationale: Wormable service exploitation enables encryption without a victim click, password submission or file launch.

entries.name: Colonial Pipeline
entries.victimPerspective: Colonial organisation at the VPN-access boundary
entries.classificationScope: Documented attacker access through the legacy single-factor VPN account
entries.rationale: This organisation-side access boundary uses already-compromised credentials and does not require fresh victim approval. How the credentials were originally acquired remains unknown.
entries.evidenceRationale: Use of the legacy single-factor VPN account is known; credential acquisition was still under investigation. No-MFA does not prove how the victim identity was first compromised.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ

entries.name: Viasat KA-SAT disruption (2022)
entries.victimPerspective: Viasat KA-SAT network operator
entries.rationale: The documented VPN-appliance misconfiguration enables entry into the trusted management segment without victim response; subsequent modem disruption is the outcome.
entries.evidenceRationale: The documented VPN-appliance misconfiguration enables entry into the trusted management segment without victim response; subsequent modem disruption is the outcome.

entries.name: Change Healthcare (Citrix portal, no MFA)
entries.victimPerspective: Change Healthcare organisation at the Citrix-access boundary
entries.classificationScope: Documented attacker access through the Citrix portal without MFA
entries.rationale: At this organisation-side portal boundary the attacker uses already-compromised credentials without fresh victim MFA approval. Credential acquisition is still not reconstructed.
entries.evidenceRationale: Ransomware, extortion and service disruption are primary. Use of compromised credentials without MFA does not establish how those credentials were acquired.
entries.uncertaintyBadge: Selected scenario — other routes may differ
